newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: Mediators seek regional force for Central Africa.
newsitem.headline: Mediators seek regional force for Central Africa.

text.p: Mediators tackling the two-month army rebellion in Central African Republic have recommended the use of African troops to separate rebel soldiers and loyalist troops and disarm civilians, a negotiator said on Thursday.

The troops would be deployed after the proposal is approved by presidents of mediation committee nations Burkina Faso, Chad, Gabon and Mali, said Colonel Alioune Ibaba, a member of the Malian-led mediation team.
"The final decision will be made by the four heads of state," Ibaba told Reuters.
He said the force would act as a buffer between mutineers and loyalists who have clashed repeatedly since the country's third mutiny in less than a year erupted on November 15.
They would also monitor peace accords and, with the help of the United Nations, disarm civilian militias loyal to President Ange-Felix Patasse, Ibaba said.

"This phase (disarmament) is not limited to members of the mediation committee," Ibaba added. "After the approval of the four heads of state, interested countries, depending on their financial, material and human resources, can participate."
Scores of people have been killed in clashes between rebels and presidential guard troops, who are backed by French forces stationed in the former colony under defence accords.

French troops fought bloody battles with rebels when they quelled a more violent mutiny in May last year, which followed an earlier one in April. Two French officers were killed in the latest uprising.

Grievances over pay and conditions turned into a campaign by predominantly southern mutineers to oust Patasse, a northerner who won elections in 1993. The mutiny has since degenerated into generalised ethnic feuding.

Mali's former military leader Amadou Toumani Toure, the chief mediator, on Thursday attended a plenary session of a consultation committee drawn from a cross section of the country's society, including leaders of opposition parties.
The session heard a report from a political subcommittee which recommended, among other things, amnesty for all Central Africans, military or civilians, involved in the mutiny.
